# v0.29.1 — compaction gets past retained rows, keeps its pause and summarises in store order

v0.29.1 is a patch release on v0.29.0. This tree is the `v0.29.1-rc4` tag plus this notes file. The release gauntlet ran at that tag; its results and any release-manager decisions are under **Qualification**, with receipts attached to this release.

It fixes three compaction problems found in v0.29.0's release testing: passes that could not cut past a row the host still holds, the 10-minute pause after such a pass ending early, and summaries that could read a leaf's rows out of store order after a host reorder. It also stops a restart after a cleanup pass from storing the conversation again (found in an earlier candidate's reference-agent window), keeps two retry shapes after a compaction to one stored copy, stores a re-stamped tool turn after a cold restart, makes the doctor's local-recall messages clearer, and fixes links in the install payload.

There are no new settings and the schema version stays 5.

## Changes since v0.29.0

### Compaction

- **Compaction gets past an unresolved retained row.** When the stored history before a row the host still holds could not be cut, every compaction pass made no progress. Compaction now summarises the blocked rows from the stored copy, up to the leaf budget, and moves on. The host's copy stays in context, so its content can appear twice but is never lost. This also works when the row sits in the protected recent turns or behind a backlog larger than one leaf, the two cases where v0.28.1's bounded escape failed. A leaf now ends before a tool group whose other half the host keeps. Each pass that uses this escape logs one WARNING naming the stored rows (IDs, role and kind only), and the `LCM compaction stop` line gains an `escaped=` field ([#1162](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1162), [#1880](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1880), [PR #2003](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2003)) After a compaction rotates the session, the new session also reads the escape records of the sessions it was compacted from (verified compression parents only), so compaction keeps making progress; the first release candidate lacked this and could stop every later pass with `selected leaf chunk lacks raw store lineage` ([#2027](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2027), [PR #2028](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2028)).
- **The 10-minute pause after a pass that changes nothing holds again.** In v0.29.0 the pause ended as soon as any new message was stored, so the next turn could run another 10–73 s pass. The running engine now waits the full 600 s, as v0.28.1 did; a restarted engine still reads the saved pause record. That record now tracks only this session's messages and summaries, so activity in another session no longer ends it. Forced, overflow, recovery and survival-ceiling compactions never wait ([#1880](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1880), [PR #2002](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2002)).
- **Summaries read a leaf's rows in store order after a host reorder.** When the host moved a stored row later in its view, the summariser could read one leaf's rows out of store order, so an older fact could follow its correction inside a summary. The summariser now reads them in store order, with each tool call before its results; a reused tool-call ID is matched by store order. Which rows a leaf covers is unchanged, and stored rows are never reordered ([#2007](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2007), [#2011](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2011), [PR #2012](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2012)).

### Restarts and retries

- **A restart after a cleanup pass no longer stores the conversation again.** A compaction pass that only cleans up the host's list (it swaps a large stored message or tool output for a short stub, or strips reasoning, and writes no summary) kept its record of the cleaned list in memory only. After a restart, LCM-X had no current record of that list, so it could fail to match the host's list and store rows it already held a second time; a message later stored out of order broke even an older record the same way. The second release candidate's reference-agent window stored 291 messages again like this, some of them more than once; this problem never loses a message. The record is now saved when the host commits the cleaned list, but only when that list replays the conversation since the last compaction: each distinct message stored since then needs its own entry in the list, and every message in the list must already be stored. A cleaned list that holds only new messages keeps its record in memory, as before. LCM-X also rewrites the saved record to match the host's current list in three cases: after a message is stored out of order, after it reconciles a batch of messages the host saved, and at a restart whose list it recognises as a replay of a session that already holds rows (for example, after an earlier version left the record stale). A restart whose first list holds only new messages does not rewrite it. A message stored in the form LCM-X replays it (a redacted tool result, for example) counts as stored, and the rewrite keeps every earlier-session row that a later summary still has to cover. If a message the record would mark as stored is not in the store, or the rewrite fails, the old record stays: that can still duplicate a message but never hides one. Two narrow cases on hosts that do not send their full history are listed under **Known issues**. v0.29.0 has the same problem ([#1286](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1286), [PR #2114](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2114); merged to main, and the release branch carries the same fix as its own commits). This fix does not stop a different, older restart problem: a cold restart of a long conversation can still store copies of some of its earlier messages, as v0.29.0 does on the same inputs; nothing is lost (see **Restarts can store old rows again** under **Known issues**, [#1674](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1674)).
- **Two retry shapes after a compaction store exactly once.** Retrying the last message after a compaction and a cold restart, or retrying a message sent right after a compaction, could store the summary text, merged into a user message, a second time at the next restart. The same record rewrite now keeps both to one copy ([#1446](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1446)).
- **A re-stamped tool turn after a cold restart is stored.** After compaction and a cold restart, if a host that gives messages no unique IDs re-sent the last assistant/tool pair with new timestamps, LCM-X could treat the pair as a retry of the stored copy and not store it. It now refuses that match when the pair's own known timestamps differ, the same rule it already applied to message IDs. This was found in an engine-level test; a trace of the supported Hermes hosts found no path that produces it ([#1967](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1967), [PR #1969](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1969)).

### Doctor and install

- **Clearer local-recall readiness.** `lcm_doctor` reports local recall as ready, preparing or unavailable, keeps model faults apart from coverage read errors, shows catch-up progress as information and a stalled or failing catch-up as a problem to act on, and names the enable command when the companion is missing. While the model is not ready, recall's `degraded` reason is one short readiness sentence; the detail stays in the doctor. A model preparation that has used up its retries tries again only from the existing background triggers, with a bounded backoff ([#1959](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1959), [PR #1976](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1976)).
- **Install payload links.** Documentation links in doctor and embedding messages use the release's version tag and fall back to `main` when the version is unknown. The payload's README drops links to pages missing from its source commit and lists them in the manifest, and the link check resolves links from the page that contains them ([#1960](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1960), [PR #1977](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1977), [PR #1985](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1985)).

### Testing improved

- **Restart tests:** 54 new restart tests, 35 of which fail on the second release candidate; two others record a known limit ([#2124](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2124), under **Known issues**). Regression tests cover the two retry shapes above, which the second release candidate's own suite records as known failures. The new tests include:
  - the reference agent's order of events: a published compaction, then a committed cleanup pass, then a message changed among later turns;
  - the first restart after an upgrade from a version that left the record stale;
  - lists that hold only new messages, with or without the system prompt in front;
  - repeated replies and turns, and a session holding an older version's duplicate copies;
  - rows stored in their replayed form;
  - a failed record rewrite;
  - a session started by a compaction.

  The exactly-once state machine now also tries retries next to a merged summary. The trace goldens record the rewrite, including at a cold restart ([PR #2114](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2114)).
- **Upgrade probe:** sessions were given a stale record the way v0.29.0 leaves one, then restarted twice, with and without redacted rows. In all 8 cases, the second restart on the third release candidate stored only its own new turn and no message a second time. v0.29.0 stores already-stored messages again at every restart.
- **Pinned-host suites:** the pinned-host fixture loads each host's real profile helpers, which clears the 12 per-host failures reported in the v0.29.0 notes; the catalog-scanner install test expects each host's own scanner verdict, and launcher paths with spaces are tested ([#1968](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1968), [#1975](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1975), [PR #1972](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1972), [PR #1979](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1979)).
- **Reliability matrix:** CI keeps and uploads each cell's re-score inputs, and the offline re-score refuses cells it cannot decide and scores stopped-turn cells ([#1987](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1987), [PR #1988](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1988), [PR #1991](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1991)).
- **Benchmark instruments:** older release trees are measured with the current instruments; benchmark producers are fixed for the local-recall default; the D1 local-recall arm gets a shared embedding cache, parallel shards and fixes for interrupt and kill races ([#1959](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1959), [#1971](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1971), [PR #1965](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1965), [PR #1973](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1973), [PR #1974](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1974), [PR #1980](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1980), [PR #1981](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1981)).
- **Compress-trace goldens and host pins:** the goldens pin the host message-ID probe, so they replay the same on hosts that give messages unique IDs, and the session-rotation case above has its own regression test ([PR #2028](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2028)). The reliability matrix pins `pyasn1` on the 0.21.x hosts after a new upstream release made those hosts install a package at start-up, which the matrix's network guard stopped ([PR #2023](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2023)).
- **Release gates:** patch releases now run the gauntlet rows their diff selects ([#1995](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1995), [PR #2008](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2008)), and the D2 facts-kept row replays a run once when the summariser service, not the product, failed ([PR #2009](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2009)).

## On by default in this release

Every change above is on by default with no new setting. Local semantic recall stays on by default, as in v0.29.0.

## Upgrade

- **Host:** Hermes 0.21.3 or newer is still required (0.21.5 or newer recommended), with Python 3.11 or newer.
- **Store:** the schema version stays 5, with no new tables, columns or triggers. The compaction escape records hashes for up to 256 rows per session in the existing session metadata (when a session started by a compaction records its own escape, it stores its compression ancestors' entries with it, within the same 256-row cap); v0.29.0 does not read that record.
- **Settings:** none added, removed or changed.
- **From v0.28.1:** follow the v0.29.0 upgrade notes first. Local semantic recall turns on at that upgrade unless you set `LCM_EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED=false`.
- **First restart after the upgrade:** a session whose saved record went stale under an earlier version (for example, a committed cleanup-only pass with no compaction since) can store its already-stored messages once more at the first restart on this version. When that restart's list replays the session, LCM-X rewrites the record to it, so later restarts do not repeat it. The old record stays when a message it would mark as stored is missing from the store. On a host whose messages carry no timestamps, LCM-X cannot recognise the replay at a restart, so the repeat can continue until the next saved record, as on v0.29.0 (see **Known issues**). Nothing is lost on a host that sends its full history at each turn, as the reference agent's host does; for a host that sends only new messages, see the repeated-message item under **Known issues** ([#2124](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2124)).
- **Rollback:** target `v0.29.0`. Take a SQLite-safe backup first (see `docs/operator-guide.md`), and compare ordered raw messages and summary provenance through upgrade, rollback and re-upgrade.

## Known issues

- **Some compaction passes still write no summary** ([#1880](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1880)): with the escape above, a pass that stalled on a retained row now writes a summary. A pass that still forms no summary input (a tool group the host keeps half of, a contiguity stop, or rows with no stored source) writes no summary but still returns a rebuilt copy of the host's list, which the host commits. Returning the host's original list on such passes is planned for v0.29.2 ([#1880](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1880)): on the reference agent, one such pass made the host rewrite its history and rebuild its prompt cache. On some long tool-heavy sessions the contiguity stop repeats on every pass, so compaction never engages and only tool-output stubbing holds the context under the threshold ([#1998](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1998)). This release retries such a pass once with a larger budget, which clears one cause; a stop at the scan limit can still repeat, and a fix is planned for a patch release. Nothing is lost. On a group whose request stays above the preflight limit and whose only progress is on hidden rows, the escape can spend about 80 to 130 s on a pass the host cannot use before a cold turn's first reply (first output came at about 95 to 162 s on the reference agent, on first turns after restarts); before the second release candidate the same group's no-op pass took about 35 s. Moving this work out of the wait before a reply is planned for v0.30.0 ([#2173](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2173)).
- **Survival-fit rotations leave no compaction record:** when a session rotates because the survival fit trimmed the live view, the new session gets no record of what the previous one compacted, so rows stored under earlier sessions may not be matched to their stored copies. A compaction that is already blocked on such rows can then stay blocked, and while it is blocked each survival fit trims older rows from what the model sees with no summary in their place (in the release-candidate case fixed above, some of those rows were not yet summarised). It was seen only together with that problem; its frequency on its own is unknown. No stored rows are lost: the store keeps every row and recall can still reach them. A fix is tracked for v0.30.0 ([#2029](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2029)).
- **Slow summaries can shrink the live view:** when summary calls time out at the compaction threshold, the survival fit can drop about 80–115 older rows from what the model sees. The store keeps every row and recall can still reach them; a fix is tracked for the compaction-you-don't-notice release ([#2004](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2004)).
- **A small context window can overflow while summaries keep failing** ([#2039](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2039)): when summary calls keep failing, the survival fit trims the live view only to about 85% of the model's window, which can be above the compaction threshold. The host can then use up its compaction attempts for that turn. A long tool-heavy turn then keeps growing until the provider rejects the request as over the window, and the session resets. It was reported on a 262,144-token local model. Stored rows are kept. The same code is in v0.29.0; a fix is planned for the next patch release.
- **Catalog install on upstream Hermes with the plugin scanner:** the upstream catalog entry pins the v0.29.0 payload until the catalog update to this release's payload lands ([Hermes #148452](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/148452)). Until then, a catalog install gets v0.29.0; use `scripts/install.sh` for this release. Hermes v0.22.6 and newer rate this release's payload `safe`: their scanner counts the small-host CPU detector's read-only `/proc/self` reads as low severity ([Hermes #146352](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/146352)). Hermes v0.22.5 and older rate it `caution` (not `safe`) for those reads; nothing was changed to hide them from the scanner ([#1946](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1946)). Hermes 0.21.3's scanner blocks a `caution` verdict from a community source, so a catalog install there needs `--force` after reviewing the findings, or `scripts/install.sh`.
- **The bundled skill cannot be opened with `skill_view`** ([#571](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/571), [#2131](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2131)): LCM-X registers its skill folder instead of the skill file, so the host's `skill_view` tool fails on every operating system (a permission error on Windows, a directory error on Linux and macOS). Capture, recall and compaction are not affected. The fix is on main and ships in v0.29.2.
- **Upstream Hermes manual `/compress`:** on Hermes stable releases up to v0.22.5, a manual `/compress` from the gateway uses the host's own compressor and bypasses LCM-X, so stored history can gain duplicate replies. No rows were lost in the reported cases. Upstream Hermes fixed this on its main branch on 2026-10-28 ([Hermes #145806](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/145806), fixing [#143587](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/143587)): `/compress` now runs the session's LCM-X engine. The fix is in Hermes canary builds from 2026-10-28 and will reach the next stable release. The LCM-X defence planned for v0.30.0 stays until the oldest supported Hermes includes the fix ([#1922](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1922), [#1924](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1924)).
- **Shutdown during a compaction** ([#2101](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2101)): if a host shuts the engine down on one thread while a compaction runs on another, that pass's uncommitted work is rolled back and the compaction fails. Nothing is corrupted, and the rows stay in the host's history. Today this can happen only when the process exits during a compaction; it matters more once hosts shut engines down at agent teardown.
- **Retry shapes still being fixed** (all are redesigned together for v0.30.0, including the two cases that can lose a row, #1837 and #1838):
  - after a tool call is retried with new message IDs, each later cold restart can store that call and its result again: one more copy per restart, nothing lost ([#1836](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1836));
  - after a cold restart, if only the tool result's message ID changes on a retry, the new result may not be stored ([#1837](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1837));
  - if the plugin restarts before a session's first compaction and the host re-sends the last tool turn with a new timestamp on its user message, that user message and its tool pair may not be stored ([#1838](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1838));
  - in some retry and restart sequences after compaction, a replaced or retried message can be dropped or stored twice ([#1451](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1451)).
  Real-host frequency is unknown.
- **Crash before a reply, then rotation:** on hosts that do not give messages unique IDs, if the agent crashes before replying and the conversation then rotates, the next turn can be stored twice. The v0.28.1 notes planned this fix for v0.29.0; it now targets v0.30.0 ([#1508](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1508)).
- **Duplicates kept on purpose:** turns stored before v0.29.0's carried-stamp marker can be stored again by a replay, and user messages that the host itself mirrors after an ACP crash recovery are kept twice. LCM-X keeps both copies rather than risk losing a genuine message; see `docs/identity-ledger.md` ([#1501](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1501), [PR #1775](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1775)).
- **Restarts can store old rows again:** at a long conversation's first turn after a gateway restart, the host rebuilds the conversation and hands its assistant and tool rows to LCM-X without their timestamps, and LCM-X can store rows it already holds a second time, as on v0.28.x and v0.29.0. Nothing is lost, but recall can show a row several times, one more copy per restart. On the reference agent this happened seven times from the install to the start of the last window (3,945 copies in all; one conversation's same 293 rows were copied at each of four restarts; one event also includes the tool result stored without its call, described below). Each event was replayed on v0.29.0 and on rc4 from the same rebuilt input (a store capture plus the pinned host code), and v0.29.0 stored the same copies, so rc4 does not make this worse. A fix is planned for v0.30.0, because it builds on the ingest record that v0.30.0 adds ([#1674](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1674)).
- **A restart can store a tool result again without its call:** at a session's first turn after a restart (a cold bind), if the point where LCM-X resumes matching falls between a tool call and its result, the result can be stored a second time without the call. Nothing is lost, and the copy is not sent to the model as a stored row (a result without its call is dropped from the model's context), but recall can show it twice. v0.29.0 behaves the same. A fix is planned for v0.29.2 ([#2163](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2163)).
- **A restart can skip a repeated tool call on hosts that reuse tool-call IDs** ([#2172](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2172)): at a session's first turn after a restart, if the host reuses tool-call IDs (for example `call_0` on every turn), a new tool call and result that repeat an earlier pair exactly can be taken for a replay and not stored. The host keeps them, but LCM-X's store does not, so recall cannot find them. Hosts that give each tool call a unique ID, as the reference agent's host does, are not affected. This was found after the release; a fix is planned for v0.29.2.
- **A crash right after a rotation can keep an extra reply in tests:** the reliability test that kills the agent right after a rotation can count one stored reply as extra. In every run checked for this release, the host had saved that reply too, so LCM-X matched the host and nothing was lost; the test's kill timing and its scorer are being fixed ([#861](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/861)). Whether the older reports in [#824](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/824) are the same test effect is still being checked.
- **Local embeddings on large, fully embedded stores (small hosts):** on a 2-CPU host with a 250,000-row fully embedded store, a semantic recall could use its full 8-second budget. Since v0.29.0, hosts with at most 2 effective CPUs answer from full text immediately when local embeddings are on by default (`degraded=true`, `cpu_limited`); explicit settings keep control. Faster exact semantic recall under contention is tracked in [#1586](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1586); the first attempt did not meet its memory bar, so no release is promised yet.
- **Local embeddings can outvote exact keyword hits:** with v0.29.0's deep-match fix, recall with embeddings off now returns its full 25 matches as well, and on the LoCoMo benchmark it answers more questions than the default local embeddings (1,165 vs 1,089 of 1,986 questions). Fusion gives the keyword arm half the weight of each embedding arm, so embedding-only hits can push an exact keyword hit out of the 25. Local embeddings still lead on LongMemEval-S (426 vs 408 of 500) and show no regression against v0.28.1. A fusion-weight change needs its own measurement and is planned for a minor release, not this patch ([#950](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/950)).
- **Python only: switching an existing config object to a cloud provider:** if code changes `embedding_provider` to a cloud provider on an `LCMConfig` that already resolved to the local default (with `dataclasses.replace` or attribute assignment), the enabled setting carries over, and that provider starts receiving text without `embeddings_enabled=True`. Settings from the environment and new `LCMConfig(...)` objects are not affected. Set `embeddings_enabled` explicitly when you switch providers in code; a fix is tracked in [#1959](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1959).
- **Subagent work is not stored:** what a delegated subagent does in its own session, including its tool calls and intermediate results, is not stored by LCM-X. Only what the subagent returns to the parent conversation is stored, so `lcm_recall` cannot find a subagent's intermediate results. This isolation is not new in this release. Storing subagent sessions is planned for v0.30.0 ([#1931](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1931)).
- **A restart at an unlucky moment around compaction can store one summary row again** ([#1286](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1286)): three narrower restart timings stay open. They are a restart after a cleanup-only pass that the host kept without signalling that it committed it; with the non-default `compression.in_place=false`, a restart after the host published the new session but before LCM-X saw it start; and a restart while a second compaction still waits for the host to adopt it. Each can store the summary text once more as a message. Nothing is lost, and all three are older than v0.29.0.
- **A repeated message on a host that does not send its full history** ([#2124](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2124)): on a host that sends its full history at each turn, as the reference agent's host does, the lists below are replays after a restart, and storing nothing is correct. On a host that sends only new messages, or only its most recent ones, a message can be lost in two narrow cases, because the saved record above can take a genuinely new message for a replay:
  - The record counts identical messages once, so a cleaned list that carries every distinct message since the last compaction, but fewer copies of a repeated one (a reply like "Done." given twice), counts as a replay of the conversation. A later batch of new messages that repeats every distinct message stored since that compaction can then be taken for a replay and not stored.
  - After a compaction, at a restart whose first list holds an older timestamped message and a new message without a timestamp, but not the rest of the session, LCM-X rewrites the record to that short list. After another restart, a new message identical to the untimestamped one, sent with the same older message, can be taken for a replay and not stored.

  Both cases come from the record this release adds; in them, v0.29.0 stores a second copy instead. Telling a replay from a genuine repeat on such hosts needs a record of which stored rows are duplicates, planned for v0.30.0.
- **Hosts whose messages carry no timestamps:** LCM-X recognises a replay at a restart only from timestamped messages. On such a host, a message inserted earlier in the list, or a list of only new unstamped messages, can still be stored again at each restart, as on v0.29.0. Nothing is lost. The reference agent's host timestamps its messages, except the assistant and tool rows it rebuilds at a restart (see the restart item above).
- **Restart duplicates the fix does not cover yet:** in a few rarer orders of events the saved record is not rewritten, so the next restart can store messages a second time, as before this fix; none loses a message ([#2115](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2115), [#2119](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2119)). When a host replaces an unstamped reply during a resend, or edits an unstamped assistant message in place, the new text is stored only at the next restart, along with a second copy of the conversation ([#2116](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2116), [#2117](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2117)). Two rarer passes that rewrite the host's list without changing which messages it holds, an overflow recovery and a compaction of only hidden rows, keep no saved record, as on v0.29.0, so a restart after one can store messages a second time ([#2134](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2134)).
- **Summary obligations after an out-of-order row in a session started by a compaction:** a later summary may not be required to cover some of the parent session's messages. The messages stay in the store and recall can still reach them. This predates v0.29.0; a fix is tracked for v0.30.0 ([#2123](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2123)).
- **Cross-process cleanup:** another process sharing the store can still clear an empty live session binding and stall later compaction ([#753](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/753), [#761](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/761)).
- **Extra rows in one degraded mode:** when a child compaction can never publish (a different case from a single failed publication), three runtime hosts store extra rows and repeat user tags. No user content is missing. That reliability cell now gates on missing content only ([#1797](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1797), [#1900](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1900), [PR #1929](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1929)).

## Qualification

- **Receipts**, attached to this release: [gauntlet summary](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/download/v0.29.1/GAUNTLET-SUMMARY.md), [Phase A](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/download/v0.29.1/PHASE-A-RECEIPT.md), [Phase B](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/download/v0.29.1/PHASE-B-RECEIPT.md) (review sweep and hands-on), [Phase C](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/download/v0.29.1/PHASE-C-RECEIPT.md), [Phase D scorecard](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/download/v0.29.1/SCORECARD-PHASE-D.md) (including the #1586 same-store row), [reference-agent window](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/download/v0.29.1/SOAK-WINDOW-RECEIPT.md), and [SHA256SUMS](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/releases/download/v0.29.1/SHA256SUMS).
- **Gauntlet tier:** as a patch release, v0.29.1 runs the rows its diff selects ([#1995](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1995)): 17 rows. Three candidates were replaced before this one: the first candidate's reliability matrix found the rotation problem fixed above, the second candidate's reference-agent window found the restart problem fixed above, and the third candidate's reliability matrix found a failed compaction in a rotated session storing LCM-X's own summary as a message (fixed in this tree; v0.29.0 does not have it). Every selected row was rerun on the fourth candidate (rc4) except the occurrence grader (see Not run); D1 LOCAL and D4/D8, which complete after this release (see Phase D); and two parts whose inputs rc4 does not change: the v0.29.0 arm of D1, and the Phase B review sweep, which covered the full diff to the third candidate and was extended by a two-family review of the one-line rc4 change.
- **Full suite, the CI way, at the rc4 SHA (59e49bf2):** PASS: CI run 41257852390 and differential run 41257854410, every job green.
- **Full suite on pinned Hermes hosts** (run 41266082132): the raw result fails on every host, and every failure is pre-existing and tracked ([#1539](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1539)): 0 new against v0.29.0 (run 40660768939). The pinned-host fixture fix cuts each host's failures from 42 to 29-30 on the floor host and three runtime hosts; the other three are unchanged at 29-30. Nine v0.29.0 tests are absent because this release removed or renamed them. An earlier run at the same commit (41259692007) had two wall-clock asserts fail, each on one host and passing on the other six; they did not recur in this full run.
- **Reliability matrix at the rc4 tag** (run 41261477146): no regression against v0.29.0 with the reliability-matrix pyasn1 pin (run 40664636011) on all 7 hosts: 0 new failing cells, and every pre-existing failing cell has a tracked issue. The failed-child-publication cell ([#541](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/541)) passes again, as on v0.29.0. A first run at the same commit (41259689966) had two errors on one host whose environment could not start the ACP server (LCM-X never ran); the rerun matches the two sibling hosts of that version exactly.
- **Phase A:** PASS: all-tools matrix and privacy batteries (38 checks: 33 tool rows, 4 batteries and the preflight; 0 failed), run in an isolated Hermes home.
- **Phase B:** CLEAR. The independent review sweep of the full v0.29.0 → rc3 diff (two model families, 32 finder runs over 4 shards; 15 unique claims, the 3 that needed it each judged by two independent lenses) found 0 confirmed defects: every claim is a known, tracked limit or is dispositioned. The one-line rc4 change and its test had their own two-family review (both approved; two non-blocking notes). The native probe matrix ran 42 cells with 0 regressions. CLEAR also rests on the pinned-host suites and the reliability matrix above (0 new failures, every pre-existing failure tracked) and on the #1501 row below (no product regression).
- **Local upgrade roundtrip** (v0.29.0 → rc4 → v0.29.0 write → rc4): PASS, 0 lost and 0 duplicated rows.
- **Local host cells** ([#1970](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1970)): no row lost in any of the four cells at rc4. Two cells are plugin-manager installs on two hosts with local embeddings. The other two are the floor host's manual setup with local embeddings, and its default setup, which runs labelled degraded full text as expected. Each cell passes the re-paste after restart, leaves the host tree unchanged and passes its doctor bar. The lossless bars are not green on three cells, and the zero-lost-rows bar is not green on the floor host's default setup. The cause is the scorers' limit on how many stored pieces they join back into one split assistant answer (2 for the older scorer, 8 for the current one), not a lost row. In one cell, a 27-tool-call answer was stored as 20 pieces, and those pieces equal the delivered answer byte for byte. Re-running the current scorer with only that limit raised passes all four cells with 0 missing and 0 duplicated rows. Compaction times are recorded, not judged.
- **Phase C live sessions** (7 pinned hosts, 45 turns each, restart and re-paste after the first compaction): every bar passes on all 7 hosts except the doctor and caught host-trace bars. Lossless v2 shows 0 missing and 0 duplicated rows on 6 of 7 hosts at its written cap; v1, which joins only two fragments, counts 1 or 2 split answers missing on 5 hosts, and v2 matches every one of them. There were 0 timeouts, and all 21 planted facts were recalled exactly (0 recoverable, 0 lost). On the floor host v2's 8-fragment cap left one answer unmatched: it was stored as 20 fragments that equal the delivered answer byte for byte. Re-scoring the same frozen evidence with only the cap raised to 64 gives 0 missing and 0 duplicated. This is the shape already ruled on for the local host cells; the raw result stays visible, and the scorer repair is a v0.29.2 kit item. The slowest compaction attempt took 97.0 s, against the 145 s bar (v0.29.0: 115.0 s). The doctor bar and the caught host-trace bar are not green. No host reports a failed check, but every host reports warnings: empty lifecycle rows on all 7, context pressure on the same two hosts as v0.29.0, and embedding-provider health on the three hosts that run labelled degraded full text. On the floor host a payload-storage warning counts one stored large tool result as missing; the file is present, and the warning comes from the replacement doctor run looking in its own empty home. Every host log has host-caught detach refusals, and the three hosts without the companion package log optional-import failures. These are the same classes as v0.29.0. Release-manager decision: [release spec](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/blob/main/bench/specs/RELEASE-READINESS-V1.md) (the "v0.29.1 only" Phase C row).
- **Local recall on a large store ([#1586](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1586)):** PASS (this measurement also serves as the offline-model recall check), no latency regression against v0.29.0, measured twice as a same-store A/B on the test Mac (200 recalls per query class per tree, in alternating blocks, against a 1.15 margin set before the first run). On rc2, with the machine to itself: every rc2/v0.29.0 ratio below 1, one-sided 95% bootstrap upper bound at most 1.003; an independent adjudicator confirmed every validity and slot condition. On rc4, with the reference agent still running and load not sampled: rc4/v0.29.0 ratios 0.995 to 1.014, upper bound at most 1.027 at p50 and p90 for both classes, and per-block medians within 3% of each other on each tree. Medians are about 1.05 s and 1.3 s per class on all three trees, with p90 at most 1.37 s on rc4. Every run had 0 timeouts and 0 errors, the same 2 degraded recalls per class on both trees, and identical coverage. This covers this Mac's covered store only, not GitHub's 2-CPU runners or customer hardware. The absolute floor bars (p50 2 s, p90 8 s on the 2-CPU floor host) stay the open #1586 limit; the floor pair was not run for this patch.
- **[#1501](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1501):** strict raw verdict FAIL against v0.29.0 on the same instrument, with no product regression: 12 cell pairs, 6 PASS, 3 FAIL, 3 UNSUPPORTED (the ACP upgrade cells, which the harness cannot drive). Two failing pairs are the duplicate shape that v0.29.0 already shows (one key-based duplicate row on both trees, 0 missing). In the third, an ACP crash test, rc4 kept the first user message of the session that followed a rotation in 1 of 4 runs (v0.29.0: 0 of 4). That message is byte for byte the host's own row, with the same ID, timestamp and position, and the host kept it in all 8 runs: the host re-merged two earlier messages into it, and LCM-X recorded it as a new version. The deciding code is unchanged from v0.29.0, which makes the same choice when given the same stored state; why that state arose in one run is not established. A review by a second model family reproduced the mechanism on both trees and found no lost, duplicated, reordered or misplaced row. The test's scorer counts such host-held rows as extra; it is being fixed ([#861](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/861)).
- **Phase D:**
  - D1 recall scorecard (OFF): PASS. LongMemEval-M, 500 questions per tree: 0 recall flips and 0 full-text flips against v0.29.0, recall@10 0.873 on both trees.

The local recall evidence before this release is the #1586 same-store row and the local-embedding host and Phase C cells; D4 LOCAL (below) also finishes after this release. D3 passes: every planted fact was admitted at all 108 final checkpoints, and no store held a level-3 node. D7 (3 runs, 186 turns after compaction): all six bars pass. There were 16.1 compactions per 100 turns (bar 25), a mean wait of 5.9 s (bar 15 s), 16.1% of turns waited (bar 25%), facts kept 0.811 (floor 0.733), 0 rows dropped, and a p90 wall time of 40.1 s (bar 120 s). The owner decided not to wait for its read ([#1286](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1286#issuecomment-6601018033)): the release rests on the D5-B store-clone cells, the seven replayed copy events and the row-by-row check below. The read runs after this release as a watch-only check, and its result goes into the v0.29.2 notes.

No rule disposes of it for window 2, so the count stays 1 lost. Also 1,623 copies (1,255 + 368); 1 LCM-X traceback and 2 LCM-X-frame log lines (the host's background review asks LCM-X to detach, LCM-X refuses, and the host catches it); the doctor's advisory about the empty lifecycle rows those reviews leave; and 41 host tool-output stubs from October whose payload files the capture does not copy. 2 of 2 turns completed.

The doctor's advisory and 10 tool-output references whose payload files the read could not find were also not green; no record was found of a check of erratum E5's limits for those two shapes at this read. One restart's replay could not start from the agent's exact state, because the capture omitted five tool-output files that only the host's own transcript referenced.
  - **Window 4** (watch-only, read after this release): it opened at a recorded restart at 04:37 UTC. The Hermes Desktop app's updater updated the host tree at 07:13 UTC, and the gateway restarted at 07:13, 07:25 and 07:59, none by the release testing (the last from the host dashboard's restart action, [recorded before the read](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1286#issuecomment-6600601099)); LCM-X stayed on the rc4 pin. The first chat turn came at 07:20, after the update, so the window observed rc4 on the newer host only. The read, after this release, counts the copies stored at the cold binds after the restarts (#1674's shape) and checks for lost rows.
  - **Rows kept:** a row-by-row check of the eleven captures from the install to window 4's start found no stored row lost or changed in identity (1,105 rows had an empty observation time filled in).
  - **The copies** are the restart problem described under known issues ([#1674](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1674)): seven events from the install to window 4's start, 3,945 copies in all, with one conversation's same 293 rows copied at each of four restarts. Each event was replayed on v0.29.0 and on rc4 from the same rebuilt input (a store capture plus the pinned host code), and v0.29.0 stored the same copies each time. This shows rc4 does not make #1674 worse. It does not show the copies are harmless.

Amendment 4 covered the install's 293 through its restart rule (no named shape covers them). Amendment 5 added the S7 rule and covered window 2's 1,255. Erratum E5 covered window 2's 368 and the 1,250 stored between the install window and window 2, ended window 2 early, and settled the 368's bind time after a failed first run. Erratum E6 covered window 3's 20: it applied replay-tool fixes to that same restart, read S7's fourth limit per copy, and recorded the owner's exception for one tool result stored again without its call ([#2163](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2163)). Erratum E7 is the release manager's decision under the owner's delegation. It covered 388 copies stored at the first turn after a recovery restart between windows 3 and 4: a restart attempt had stopped itself because another profile's gateway held the agent's store (a cross-profile issue, tracked in [#2152](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2152)). E7 also re-read the no-later-bind limit for window 3's 371 after that limit had failed, and changed the classifier during window 4. Errata E1 to E4 only made amendment 4 stricter, before window 2. All are on [#1286](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1286), with corrections in [one later comment](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1286#issuecomment-6598125537). Window 4's read rule and the decision not to wait for its read were both made before the read.
  - **D5-B store-clone cells:** two cells of 44 turns each, with 0 timeouts. Every bar passes (0 missing and 0 duplicated rows over 88 keys, restart and re-paste, 3 of 3 probes exact, slowest compaction attempt 61.8 s against the 145 s bar) except the doctor and LCM-X-frame traceback bars, as on v0.29.0. The doctor gives three warnings (config_validation, embedding_provider_health and lifecycle_fragmentation; 0 failed checks), and the cells have 8 and 6 traces with an LCM-X frame, every one the host-caught refusal to detach a background-review fork.

**Release-manager decisions.**
- v0.29.0's notes listed seven rows that were not green and said each would run again in this release and must pass or carry a new disclosed decision. Two now pass: D2/D3, after a passing prospective A/A check, and the Phase B host suites and reliability matrix, where every pre-existing failure now has a tracked issue. The rest are below.
- **D1 LOCAL and D4/D8:** not run before this release (raw verdict UNRUN; not green), by new decisions (see the Phase D lines). Both run after this release, with results in the v0.29.2 notes; a D4 or D8 failure becomes a priority fix for v0.29.2. D8 runs again, as v0.29.0's notes required, but finishes after this release; this is the new disclosed decision they asked for.
- **D8 rule:** from v0.29.2's first release candidate, D8 is planned to use a count-margin rule calibrated on this release's LOCAL runs ([PR #2097](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2097)).
- **Reference-agent window (D5):** the three reads before window 4 are raw FAILs with no decision, and D5 is not green. Each rule that disposed of their copies or ended a window was written after seeing the data it judges (see the reference-agent line under Qualification, which lists them; all are on [#1286](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1286)). The owner made the exception in erratum E6 and delegated erratum E7 to the release manager. Window 4 was interrupted by a Hermes host update at 07:13 UTC and three gateway restarts, none by the release testing (LCM-X stayed on rc4), so it cannot decide. Under the rule posted before its read ([#1286](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1286#issuecomment-6598125537)), its read became a watch-only check that could stop the release only on a confirmed lost row caused by rc4; the owner then decided, also before the read, not to wait for it ([#1286](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1286#issuecomment-6601018033)). The release rests on the D5-B cells, the seven replayed copy events and the row-preservation chain, and the read's result goes into the v0.29.2 notes. None of the three reads before this release recorded an organic compaction published to the host (0 in each), so compaction under real use is not covered by this release's windows.
- **Phase C doctor bar and caught host-trace bar:** not green, as on v0.29.0, by the disclosed decision above.
- **D5-B doctor and LCM-X-frame traceback bars:** not green, as on v0.29.0, by a disclosed decision ([PR #2081](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2081)).
- **Occurrence grader:** selected for this patch but not run, because the test machine lacked the disk space it needs. Moving it to a larger host is a v0.29.2 kit item.
- **[#1501](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1501):** the strict raw verdict is FAIL with no product regression (above). The test fix and its scorer gap are tracked in [#861](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/861); an occurrence-aware compose is an accepted follow-up, revisited at the v0.30.0 exactly-once design ([#1993](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1993)).
- **Release candidates rc2 and rc3:** both were replaced before this release. rc3 added a duplicate-row fix ([#2114](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2114)); its reliability matrix then found a regression from that fix ([#2128](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2128)), and rc4 adds a one-line fix for it ([#2132](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2132)) that passed the matrix 7/7 before the tag. Every selected row ran again at rc4 except the occurrence grader (not run), D1 LOCAL and D4/D8 (they complete after this release; raw UNRUN, not green), and two carried parts: v0.29.0's D1 OFF arm, and the Phase B review sweep (run at rc3, plus a two-family review of the rc4 change). Accepted tradeoff: after two rare passes (an overflow recovery and a compaction of only hidden rows), the restart behaviour goes back to v0.29.0's ([#2134](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2134)).
- **Local host cells:** the lossless bars are not green on three cells because of a scorer limit on split assistant answers; an uncapped re-score of the same frozen evidence finds no missing and no duplicated row (above). The same limit left one answer unmatched in the floor host's Phase C session, with the same uncapped result (above). The scorer fix goes into v0.29.2.
- **#1586 at rc4:** PASS, but the rc4 run had the reference agent running and load not sampled (disclosed above).
- **Reference-agent install:** while the reference agent was stopped for the install, another profile's gateway ran three of its scheduled jobs (upstream Hermes bugs, reported). They failed without writing anything, the stores were unchanged, and their failure notices reached the agent's owner.
- **Test-kit fixes during the run** (instrument changes only; no product change and no row result changed):
  - three bench input files were restored after a kit-build rename slip;
  - launches that stopped before any test ran, because of a missing setting or tool path, were re-run under new row names;
  - the host-cell snapshot was told to skip a regenerable download cache;
  - the #1501 comparison was pointed at the runner's real output folder;
  - the D4 rows ran with v0.29.0's tool path.
- **[#1967](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1967):** found in an engine-level test only; the fix ships in this release ([PR #1969](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1969)), and the issue stays open under v0.30.0 with the other retry-shape work ([#1993](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1993)).

**Corrections, 2026-11-03, after publication:**
- The catalog item under **Known issues** first said the catalog entry pinned v0.28.1 (it pins v0.29.0), and it gave only the older scanner verdict.
- The restart-copies item first said its fix was planned for v0.29.2. That fix builds on the ingest record that v0.30.0 adds, so it is planned for v0.30.0.
